subject: agrad as a lib outside of Stan?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: agrad as a lib outside of Stan?
parts:
Can anyone enlighten me as to how to compile a standalone
C++ program against Stan's agrad lib? If it can't be done,
I'll submit an issue and we can add it to our to-do list.

I get this behavior (Mac OSX, latest OS, latest Xcode clang++):

|
~/temp2/eigencopy$ clang++ -O3 -I ~/stan/lib/eigen_3.1.3 -I ~/stan/src -I ~/stan/lib/boost_1.53.0 var.cpp -L ~/stan/bin
Undefined symbols for architecture x86_64:
"stan::agrad::var_stack_", referenced from:
_main in var-0kEmYM.o
"stan::agrad::memalloc_", referenced from:
_main in var-0kEmYM.o
ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture x86_64
clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1 (use -v to see invocation)
|

when compiling this var.cpp file:

|
#include <iostream>
#include <stan/agrad/agrad.hpp>

using namespace stan::agrad;

int main() {
var a = 1;
std::cout << a;
}
|

- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] agrad as a lib outside of Stan?
parts:
This is an easy fix. For the library inclusion flag, -L, it should be:
-L ~/stan/bin -l stan

instead of just
-L ~/stan/bin

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] agrad as a lib outside of Stan?
parts:
To compile your code, you need add -lstan to the end of your command.  But I am not sure that is your goal.  

A related question is can we make our math a standalone library, at least not requiring our agrad. I have reported this here, https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-dev/Qicax2XZmFo/yEQ5BCyM8JQJ

--
Jiqiang
